artists.biography: Pure Reason Revolution is a British rock group formed at the University of Westminster in 2003. Their music incorporates elements of progressive rock and electronic. Members have a shared appreciation for the work of bands such as Pink Floyd, Porcupine Tree, Nirvana, Justice, Kraftwerk and Fleetwood Mac.

perplexity.description:
The Dark Third is the debut studio album by British progressive rock band Pure Reason Revolution, released in April 2006. Produced by Paul Northfield—known for his work with Rush, Porcupine Tree, and Gentle Giant—the album was recorded at Fairhazel Studios and RAK Studios, establishing the band's sophisticated approach to progressive rock composition. The album's title derives from the concept of the "dark third," referring to the third of a person's life spent asleep and dreaming, with thematic exploration evident throughout, particularly in the track "In Aurelia" on the second disc, which draws inspiration from Gérard de Nerval's novel Aurelia.

Musically, The Dark Third synthesizes influences from classic progressive rock and art rock traditions, drawing comparisons to Pink Floyd, Porcupine Tree, Marillion, and Led Zeppelin. The album showcases intricate melodies, complex arrangements, and distinctive vocal harmonies that became hallmarks of the band's sound. With a runtime of 55 minutes and 31 seconds, the album presents an expansive sonic landscape characteristic of the progressive rock genre.

The album received positive critical reception upon its release, with reviewers and listeners praising its ambitious songwriting and musicianship. It marked Pure Reason Revolution's transition from their earlier EP releases to a full-length statement, establishing them within the contemporary progressive rock scene. The album was subsequently released in Europe by InsideOut Music in February 2007 with bonus material, and has maintained a dedicated following within progressive rock circles.
